# MidwayBuyer

<!-- generated by scripts/render.mjs from data/ ; do not edit -->

Application-facing front door for FWA pack acquisition, status, settlement, and reward         claims. The only address an integrator indexes.

**Address**: not yet deployed. `midway-v1` is pending deployment.
**Source**: `src/midway/MidwayBuyer.sol`

## Functions

### State changing

| Function | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| `acceptOwner()` |  |
| `acquire()` | Acquires one FWA pack for the caller's application under the application's saved         settlement default. Quotes inside the call and returns ETH above the quote to the         caller. |
| `acquire(bool)` | Acquires with an explicit settlement default for this request. `autoSettleEth` true         lets a permissionless caller drive the request to ETH; false keeps the outcome for         the account. |
| `autoResolve(uint256[])` | Drives each request to its terminal outcome. Permissionless. Reads no price. |
| `claimAccruedRewards(uint256[],uint256)` | Claims accrued FWA rewards for each request. The engine derives the swap bound from         pool spot; `minOut` may only tighten it. Permissionless. |
| `claimEpochRewards(uint256[],uint256[])` | Claims closed-epoch FWA purchaser rewards. Permissionless: the destination is the         registry-named recipient of each request's application and no caller can redirect it.         `midwayRequestIds[i]` is claimed for `epochs[i]`; repeat an id to claim several epochs. |
| `deliverNFT(uint256,address)` |  |
| `makeManaged(uint256)` | Sets this request's `autoSettleEth` to true. One way; reverts `AlreadyManaged` when         it is already true. Account or account operator. |
| `payoutRewards(uint256[],uint8)` | Pays each application's full `kind` pot out to its registry-named recipient.         Permissionless: the recipient is resolved by the registry, not by the caller. Skips         an application whose pot is empty. |
| `proposeOwner(address)` |  |
| `recoverForcedOutcome(uint256[])` | Classifies each request whose FWA outcome was forced and records the resulting         incident. Permissionless; called by Midway's keeper. |
| `recoverStuckNFT(uint256[])` | Recovers an NFT stuck on a request's clone into the request's incident record.         Permissionless; called by Midway's keeper. |
| `rescueEth(address)` | Recovers ETH mis-sent to the router. Sends the full balance: the router never holds         ETH as part of an acquisition, so any balance here is stray. |
| `rescueNFT(address,uint256,address)` | Recovers an ERC721 mis-sent to the router. |
| `rescueToken(address,address,uint256)` | Recovers an ERC20 mis-sent to the router. The router holds no protocol funds itself;         every acquisition's ETH and reward flow routes through the engine, request buyer, and         reward vault instead. |
| `retrySharedUpsideActivity(uint256[])` | Retries a pending Shared Upside activity record for each request. Permissionless;         called by Midway's keeper. |
| `setAcquisitionsPaused(bool)` |  |
| `setActiveEngine(address)` |  |
| `setMidwayFeeConfig((uint16,address))` |  |
| `settleForEth(uint256[])` | Settles for ETH: accepts FWA's depositor bid and pays the recorded account.         Permissionless; the payout target is the snapshotted account. |
| `settleForFwat(uint256,uint256)` | Settles for FWAT under the caller's own `minOut` and deposits the result into the         application's RewardVault pot. Account or account operator. Reverts         `FwatSettlementUnavailable` when the RewardVault is not a FWAToken distributor. |
| `syncRequest(uint256[])` |  |
| `withdrawRefunds(uint256[])` | Withdraws the fee-reserve refund of each finalized request to its recorded account. |

<details>
<summary>`deliverNFT(uint256,address)`</summary>

Reads the delivered collection and token id from the request's incident record when one      exists (a recovered forced or stuck asset), otherwise from FWA's listing (a fulfilled      allocation).

</details>

<details>
<summary>`syncRequest(uint256[])`</summary>

Every batched lifecycle verb below splits ids across the distinct engines they route      to, calls each engine once, and zips the per-engine `LifecycleOutcome[]` results back      into original call order via `_distinctEnginesIndexed` and a per-engine cursor. No      verb makes a view call into the engine; every emitted event reads only the outcome the      engine already returned.

</details>
